chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning

A man who performed salat (prayer) and did not know whether he had prayed two, or three, or four; he said: “Then he stands and performs two rakʿahs standing and gives salām, then he performs two rakʿahs sitting and gives salām. So if it was four rakʿahs, then the two rakʿahs will be supererogatory; otherwise, the four are completed.”

And whoever doubts and does not know whether he prayed one, or two, or three, or four, then repeating the salat (prayer) is obligatory upon him, because the first two rakʿahs were not secured for him. We have already indicated that whoever does not have the first two rakʿahs secured for him, it is obligatory upon him to restart the salat (prayer). This is also indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat (prayer) if he doubts whether he prayed two, three, or four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This report discusses rulings for doubt in the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer). If the doubt is between two, three, and four, compensatory rakʿahs are performed; but if the uncertainty includes even the possibility of having prayed only one rakʿah, the salat (prayer) must be repeated because the first two rakʿahs are not established with certainty.
